title: 2014 AMC 12B Problem 13
statement: Real numbers \(a\) and \(b\) are chosen with \(1 \lt a \lt b\) such that no triangle with positive area has side lengths \(1,\) \(a,\) and \(b\) or \(\tfrac1b,\) \(\tfrac1a,\) and \(1.\) What is the smallest possible value of \(b?\)

solutions.text:
Since \(b\) is the largest of \(1, a, b,\) no such triangle exists exactly when \(b \ge a+1.\) Since \(1\) is the largest of \(\tfrac1b, \tfrac1a, 1,\) no such triangle exists exactly when \(1 \ge \tfrac1a + \tfrac1b,\) that is \(a \le \tfrac{b}{b-1}.\)

Both conditions hold with \(b\) smallest when \(a+1 = b\) and \(a = \tfrac{b}{b-1}\) meet, giving \(b - 1 = \tfrac{b}{b-1},\) or \(b^2 - 3b + 1 = 0.\)

The root larger than \(1\) is \(b = \dfrac{3+\sqrt5}{2}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: With \(1 \lt a \lt b,\) no triangle \(1, a, b\) means \(b \ge a+1\)
